identity.title: Reasoning with Sampling: Your Base Model is Smarter Than You Think

problem.claim: Whether base models can yield reasoning capabilities comparable to RL-posttrained models at inference time through pure sampling, without additional training.

gap.claim: The abstract frames prior work as focused largely on separating genuinely novel RL-emergent behaviors from capabilities already present in base models, leaving inference-time elicitation via sampling as an alternative question.

contributions.claim: An iterative sampling algorithm inspired by MCMC that uses base-model likelihoods to elicit reasoning at inference time without additional training.

Across different base models, the authors report reasoning boosts nearly matching or outperforming RL on single-shot MATH500, HumanEval, and GPQA tasks, while avoiding RL-associated multi-sample diversity collapse.
The method requires no training, curated datasets, or verifier, which the authors suggest may support application beyond easily verifiable domains.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by eliciting reasoning from base models through pure inference-time sampling rather than additional RL training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, across different base models, the sampler substantially boosts reasoning and nearly matches or exceeds RL on single-shot MATH500, HumanEval, and GPQA.
The authors report that the sampler avoids the multi-sample diversity collapse they characterize as typical of RL posttraining.

narrative_sequence.summary: RL-posttrained frontier reasoning models are described as highly capable across disciplines.
The literature is described as investigating which behaviors emerge during RL rather than already existing in base models.
The paper asks whether base-model reasoning comparable to RL can be elicited at inference time by pure sampling without training.
The authors propose an MCMC-inspired iterative sampler based on the base model’s likelihoods.
They report near-parity or gains over RL on three single-shot tasks, preserved diversity across samples, and no need for training, curated data, or a verifier.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a capability comparison with explicit operating constraints: no training, curated datasets, or verifier, plus behavior across multiple base models and tasks.

lessons.interpretation: This makes the claim easier to assess as both a performance question and a deployment-scope question.
lessons.application: Frame a method contribution with named benchmarks or settings alongside the resources and assumptions it does not require.
lessons.exception: Avoid broad scope claims when the abstract does not identify the tested domains, model coverage, or conditions behind them.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify base models, RL baselines, numerical results, sampling budgets, statistical uncertainty, or exact diversity metrics.
The stated applicability beyond easily verifiable domains is a suggestion, not a demonstrated result in the supplied units.
The abstract does not establish priority or independently verify the claimed comparisons.
